children.title: Pricing Effort-Progress Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: The tradeoff between candidate-evaluation effort and achieved progress.

children.title: Pricing Evaluation Overhead
children.top_down_role: Cost of evaluating or maintaining candidate information during pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Evaluation Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Candidate-evaluation accounting for full, partial, or sampled pricing under a fixed reduced-cost implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a standard-form linear program with \(n\) variables and basis size \(m\). If pricing at iteration \(k\) constructs a set \(C_k\) of nonbasic candidate variables and evaluates each \(j\in C_k\) at cost \(e_{kj}\), define its work by \[W_k^{\mathrm{price}}=h_k+\sum_{j\in C_k}e_{kj},\] where \(h_k\) is the candidate-set construction overhead. If there are constants \(0<c_1\le c_2\), independent of \(j\in C_k\), such that \(c_1e_k\le e_{kj}\le c_2e_k\), then \(W_k^{\mathrm{price}}=h_k+\Theta(|C_k|e_k)\). Full pricing takes \(C_k\) to be the set of all \(n-m\) nonbasic variables; partial or sampled pricing uses a smaller candidate set. Reduced immediate pricing work alone does not determine total algorithmic work because the selected entering variable can affect subsequent progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing overhead is candidate-set construction work plus the costs of evaluating the selected nonbasic candidates. Full pricing examines all n−m nonbasic variables, whereas partial or sampled pricing examines fewer; immediate savings do not by themselves determine total work.
assumptions_latex: The linear program is in standard form with \(n\) variables and basis size \(m\).
At iteration \(k\), pricing evaluates a candidate set \(C_k\) of nonbasic variables.
Evaluating candidate \(j\in C_k\) incurs nonnegative work \(e_{kj}\), and constructing \(C_k\) incurs nonnegative work \(h_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_k^{\mathrm{price}}=h_k+\sum_{j\in C_k}e_{kj}\); under uniform-order evaluation costs, \(W_k^{\mathrm{price}}=h_k+\Theta(|C_k|e_k)\).

children.title: Pricing-Induced Progress
children.top_down_role: Progress characteristics associated with the candidates selected by a pricing policy.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Induced Progress
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic primal-simplex objective progress, including the possibility of a degenerate pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each admissible entering index \(j\), let \(d=B^{-1}A_j\) and \(\theta_j=\min_{i:d_i>0}(x_B)_i/d_i\). Replacing a leaving basic variable selected by this ratio test and increasing \(x_j\) from \(0\) to \(\theta_j\) changes the objective by \[c^\top x^{+}-c^\top x=\theta_j\bar c_j.\] Hence the pricing-induced objective progress is \(P_j=-\theta_j\bar c_j\ge 0\). Because \(\bar c_j<0\), this progress is strictly positive exactly when \(\theta_j>0\), and it is zero for a degenerate pivot with \(\theta_j=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An improving priced column yields objective reduction equal to its feasible step times the negative reduced cost; the reduction is positive for a positive step and zero for a degenerate pivot.
assumptions_latex: The primal LP is \(\min\{c^\top x:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and the current basis matrix \(B\) is nonsingular with \(x_B=B^{-1}b\ge0\).
A nonbasic index \(j\) has column \(A_j\), reduced cost \(\bar c_j<0\), transformed direction \(d=B^{-1}A_j\), and at least one component \(d_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pivot decreases the objective by \(P_j=-\theta_j\bar c_j\ge0\), and \(P_j>0\) if and only if \(\theta_j>0\).

notation.meaning: Maximum feasible step for entering variable j
Objective improvement produced by the pivot

children.title: Evaluation-to-Progress Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Balance between additional pricing effort versus the resulting pivot progress.

assumptions_latex: At an iteration, \(J\) is the finite set of pivot candidates examined by a pricing procedure.
Each examined candidate \(j\) has evaluation cost \(E_j>0\) and predicted progress \(P_j\ge 0\), measured in fixed common units.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cost-aware pricing choice may be defined by maximizing \(P_j/E_j\), while its nondominated alternatives form the Pareto frontier of \((E_j,-P_j)\).

notation.meaning: Computational effort required to evaluate candidate j
Predicted progress per unit evaluation effort

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal per-iteration cost-effectiveness criterion, not a universal optimality claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Candidate \(k\in J\) dominates candidate \(j\in J\) in the evaluation-to-progress comparison when \(E_k\le E_j\) and \(P_k\ge P_j\), with at least one strict inequality. The nondominated candidates constitute the Pareto frontier. After fixing the units of effort and progress, the scalar cost-effectiveness score \[\rho_j=\frac{P_j}{E_j}\] defines one implementable tradeoff rule: choose any \(j^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{j\in J}\rho_j\). Rescaling either metric changes this scalarization but does not change Pareto dominance under positive rescaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing candidates can be compared by evaluation cost and predicted progress; maximizing progress per unit cost is one explicit scalar tradeoff rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation-to-Progress Tradeoff

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto definitions are coherent and the principle fits the tradeoff leaf, but the progress-per-evaluation-cost pricing rule is a specialized policy with no cited source.

children.title: Sparsity-Reliability Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Fill, vector density, and factorization-health consequences of pivot choices.

children.title: Pivot-Induced Sparsity
children.top_down_role: Effects of pivot choices on fill, vector density, plus basis-update structure.

assumptions_latex: A basis change replaces column \(A_{B(r)}\) by \(A_j\), where \(B\) is nonsingular and \(d=B^{-1}A_j\) satisfies \(d_r\ne0\).
Sparsity is measured by the number of structurally nonzero entries in an update vector or updated representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pivot's local update sparsity is quantified by \(s_j=\lVert d\rVert_0\); smaller \(s_j\) permits a sparser elementary basis update, although later fill depends on update ordering and factorization.

notation.meaning: Pivot column expressed in current basis coordinates
Number of structurally nonzero entries of d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural sparsity of a single revised-simplex basis update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_r\) be the coordinate vector of the leaving position and define \(T=I+(d-e_r)e_r^T\). The updated basis satisfies \[B^+=BT,\qquad T e_r=d.\] Thus the nonidentity part of this elementary basis transformation is supported only in column \(r\), with structural support determined by \(d-e_r\). The quantity \(s_j=\lVert d\rVert_0\) therefore measures pivot-induced update sparsity. It describes the immediate update, not the eventual nonzero count of accumulated factors, which can also depend on cancellation, ordering, and refactorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonzero pattern of the transformed entering column controls the immediate sparsity of an elementary basis update, but not all later factorization fill.
knowledge_statements.title: Pivot-Induced Sparsity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The elementary transformation formula is consistent, but no source supports identifying \(\lVert d\rVert_0\) as the pivot-induced sparsity metric. Its nonidentity support is actually determined by \(d-e_r\), so the convention needs authoritative support or clarification.

children.title: Pivot Numerical Reliability
children.top_down_role: Effects of pivot choices on numerical trustworthiness plus factorization health.

assumptions_latex: A candidate pivot uses transformed column \(d=B^{-1}A_j\) and leaving position \(r\) with \(d_r\ne0\).
A scale \(\sigma_j>0\) and acceptance threshold \(\tau\in(0,1]\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scale-aware test \(|d_r|\ge\tau\sigma_j\) defines an admissible numerically reliable pivot; failure rejects or penalizes that candidate.

notation.meaning: Chosen magnitude scale for the transformed column

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational relative-pivot test; the scale and tolerance are implementation parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a scale such as \(\sigma_j=\lVert d\rVert_\infty\). The candidate pair \((j,r)\) satisfies the relative numerical-reliability condition precisely when \[|d_r|\ge \tau\sigma_j.\] Since the elementary update uses divisions by \(d_r\), the reciprocal amplification indicator \(\kappa_{j,r}=\sigma_j/|d_r|\) obeys \(\kappa_{j,r}\le1/\tau\) for every accepted pivot. This condition does not certify the conditioning of the complete basis; it only excludes pivot elements that are small relative to the selected local scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pivot is locally acceptable when its pivot element is not too small relative to the transformed column scale, limiting division amplification.
knowledge_statements.title: Pivot Numerical Reliability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local amplification inequality follows from the proposed threshold, but calling this implementation-defined test numerical reliability requires a source specifying the scale and tolerance convention.

children.title: Sparsity-Reliability Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Cases where preserving sparse structure conflicts with numerically preferable pivot choices.

assumptions_latex: Each admissible pivot \(p\) has a sparsity cost \(s(p)\ge0\) and reliability margin \(q(p)>0\), computed under fixed conventions.
Both metrics are compared within the same simplex iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A pivot is tradeoff-efficient exactly when no admissible alternative has both weakly smaller sparsity cost and weakly larger reliability margin, with one strict improvement.

notation.meaning: Predicted structural cost or fill measure for pivot p

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto formulation of a local implementation tradeoff.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For admissible pivots \(p\) and \(p'\), say that \(p'\) dominates \(p\) when \(s(p')\le s(p)\) and \(q(p')\ge q(p)\), with at least one strict inequality. The sparsity-reliability frontier is the set of nondominated pivots. A scalar policy may choose \[p^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{p}\bigl(s(p)-\lambda q(p)\bigr),\qquad \lambda\ge0,\] but the selected pivot depends on \(\lambda\). Consequently, sparsity alone or reliability alone does not determine a unique tradeoff choice unless one metric is imposed as a constraint or a scalarization is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Efficient pivots are those for which no alternative is simultaneously sparser and more reliable; a unique choice requires a constraint or weighting.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Reliability Tradeoff

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto formulation is internally coherent and fits the tradeoff container, but the selected sparsity and reliability metrics and their scalarization have no supporting citation.

children.title: Tableau Pivot Control
children.top_down_role: Pivot decisions represented through explicit tableau information.

assumptions_latex: The LP is in standard minimization form with a primal-feasible nonsingular basis \(B\).
The tableau convention stores \(B^{-1}A\), \(B^{-1}b\), and reduced costs \(\bar c^T=c^T-c_B^TB^{-1}A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Entering and leaving decisions, the pivot update, and the new basic solution are determined directly from the displayed tableau quantities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-simplex control using a full explicit tableau.

source_refs.locator: 3.8 The Simplex Method in Tableau Format p. 125

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The tableau represents the current dictionary by \[x_B=B^{-1}b-B^{-1}A_Nx_N,\qquad c^Tx=c_B^TB^{-1}b+\bar c_N^Tx_N.\] For minimization, an index \(j\in N\) with \(\bar c_j<0\) may enter. With \(d=B^{-1}A_j\), the leaving position is any minimizer of \((x_B)_i/d_i\) over \(d_i>0\). A Gauss-Jordan pivot on the displayed element \(d_r\) updates every tableau row and makes the selected entering variable basic. If no \(d_i>0\), the improving direction is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full tableau explicitly displays basic values, transformed columns, and reduced costs, so pricing, ratio testing, and pivot updating use its entries directly.

children.title: Revised-Simplex Pivot Control
children.top_down_role: Pivot decisions represented through basis solves and reduced information.

assumptions_latex: The LP is \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\ge0\}\) with a primal-feasible nonsingular basis \(B\).
Linear systems with \(B\) and \(B^T\) can be solved from a maintained basis factorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The revised-simplex iteration reproduces tableau pivot decisions without explicitly forming the complete tableau.

notation.meaning: Reduced cost of nonbasic column j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One primal revised-simplex iteration in exact arithmetic.

source_refs.locator: 5.1 The Revised Simplex Method p. 201

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with \(x_B=B^{-1}b\). Solve \(B^Ty=c_B\), compute \(\bar c_j=c_j-A_j^Ty\) for priced nonbasic indices, and stop as optimal if every \(\bar c_j\ge0\). Otherwise select \(j\) with \(\bar c_j<0\), solve \(Bd=A_j\), and stop as unbounded if \(d_i\le0\) for every \(i\). Select \[r\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{i:d_i>0}\frac{(x_B)_i}{d_i},\] replace the leaving basis column by \(A_j\), update or refactor the basis representation, recompute the basic solution, and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Revised simplex obtains pricing and ratio-test data from basis solves, updating only the basis representation rather than the full tableau.

children.top_down_role: Pricing represented through simplex multipliers and reduced costs.

assumptions_latex: The LP is in standard minimization form and \(B\) is a nonsingular current basis.
The basic-cost vector is \(c_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pricing is represented by one transposed basis solve followed by column products: \(\bar c_j=c_j-y^TA_j\).

notation.meaning: Simplex multiplier satisfying the transposed basis system

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier representation of primal-simplex pricing.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the transposed basis system \[B^Ty=c_B.\] Then every column \(A_j\) has reduced cost \(\bar c_j=c_j-y^TA_j\). For a primal-feasible basis in a minimization problem, \(\bar c_j<0\) identifies an improving nonbasic candidate, while \(\bar c_j\ge0\) for all nonbasic indices certifies optimality. Thus one multiplier vector supports pricing over any subset of columns without forming \(B^{-1}A\) in full; only the chosen column must subsequently be transformed for the ratio test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplex multiplier from one transposed basis solve gives every reduced cost through a column inner product and supports partial or full pricing.

children.title: Stable-Pivot Preferences
children.top_down_role: Pivot choices influenced by anticipated basis-update reliability.

assumptions_latex: At a primal-feasible iteration, \(P\) is the finite set of pivots passing the sign and ratio-test requirements.
Each pivot \(p\in P\) has progress score \(g(p)\ge0\) and scale-normalized stability margin \(q(p)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A stable-pivot preference restricts selection to \(q(p)\ge\tau\) or explicitly penalizes small \(q(p)\), without altering feasibility requirements.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A configurable pivot-ranking condition, not a basis-conditioning theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\tau>0\), define the stable admissible set \[P_\tau=\{p\in P:q(p)\ge\tau\}.\] If \(P_\tau\ne\varnothing\), a thresholded stable-pivot policy chooses a pivot from \(P_\tau\), for example one maximizing \(g(p)\). An alternative soft preference selects a maximizer of \(g(p)-\lambda/q(p)\) for \(\lambda\ge0\). In either form, the stability measure changes the ranking only among pivots already admissible under the simplex feasibility and improvement rules; it cannot make an infeasible pivot admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stable-pivot preferences filter or penalize candidates using a local stability margin while retaining the ordinary feasibility and improvement tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Stable-Pivot Preferences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The threshold and penalty rules are coherent policy examples, but the stability metric and ranking policy are uncited. The record also mixes an admissibility condition with a soft preference policy, making the selected condition kind uncertain.

children.title: Refactorization-Policy Interface
children.top_down_role: Changes in pricing or acceptance policy around basis refactorization.

children.title: Basis Refactorization Events
children.top_down_role: Factorization-replacement events relevant to simplex pivot control.

assumptions_latex: A revised-simplex implementation maintains an updated factorization or product-form representation of a nonsingular basis \(B_k\).
A monitored trigger predicate \(R_k\) is available after iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A basis refactorization event occurs when \(R_k\) is true and replaces the accumulated representation by a fresh factorization of the same basis matrix.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event semantics independent of the particular trigger or sparse factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A basis refactorization event at iteration \(k\) is the operation performed when \(R_k\) is true: discard the accumulated update representation, compute a fresh numerical factorization \(F_k\) of the unchanged current basis \(B_k\), and use \(F_k\) for subsequent solves with \(B_k\) and \(B_k^T\). In exact arithmetic the represented basis and basic solution are unchanged. Typical predicates may depend on update count, solve residuals, estimated conditioning, or fill, but the choice of \(R_k\) is part of the implementation policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A refactorization event rebuilds a fresh factorization of the current basis when a trigger fires, without changing the represented basis in exact arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Refactorization Events

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the event container and is plausible, but the trigger examples and claims about discarded update representations and subsequent solves require an inspectable implementation source.

children.title: Post-Refactorization Pivot Policy
children.top_down_role: Pricing or acceptance policies used following basis refactorization.

assumptions_latex: A fresh factorization of the current basis has just been computed.
Pricing and feasibility quantities are recomputed consistently from that factorization using prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next pivot is selected from freshly recomputed admissible candidates; stale pre-refactorization transformed columns and reduced costs are not reused as authoritative values.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restart policy immediately following a numerical basis refactorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After refactorization, solve \(Bx_B=b\) and \(B^Ty=c_B\) using the fresh factors. Recompute required reduced costs \(\bar c_j=c_j-A_j^Ty\), reapply feasibility and optimality tolerances, and construct the current admissible pivot set \(P^{\mathrm{new}}\). If \(P^{\mathrm{new}}\) is empty, return the status implied by the recomputed tests. Otherwise select a pivot from \(P^{\mathrm{new}}\), transform its entering column with the fresh factors, perform the ratio test, and update the basis. Quantities tied to the discarded update representation must be recomputed or explicitly validated before reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Immediately after refactorization, recompute basic values, multipliers, and candidate tests from fresh factors before selecting the next pivot.
knowledge_statements.title: Post-Refactorization Pivot Policy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the post-refactorization policy leaf, but mandatory recomputation and restrictions on reusing stored quantities are implementation claims with no citation.

children.title: Pre-Refactorization Pivot Policy
children.top_down_role: Pricing or acceptance adjustments used as refactorization approaches.

assumptions_latex: The current basis is represented by accumulated numerical updates and a refactorization predicate \(R_k\) can be evaluated.
Candidate pivots satisfy the ordinary simplex admissibility tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When refactorization is imminent, the policy either refactorizes before pivoting or accepts only a candidate satisfying an explicitly strengthened stability test.

notation.meaning: Local stability margin of pivot p

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guard policy for pivot selection when accumulated basis updates approach replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Evaluate \(R_k\) before committing the next basis change. If \(R_k\) is false, apply the ordinary pivot rule. If \(R_k\) is true, either refactorize immediately and defer selection to the post-refactorization policy, or form \[P_{\mathrm{pre}}=\{p\in P_k:q_k(p)\ge\tau_{\mathrm{pre}}\}.\] Under the latter option, pivot only if \(P_{\mathrm{pre}}\ne\varnothing\), select within that set by the prescribed progress rule, and refactorize after the update; if the set is empty, refactorize before any pivot. The threshold and trigger are implementation parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before an imminent refactorization, either rebuild first or permit only pivots meeting a strengthened local stability threshold, then rebuild after the update.
knowledge_statements.title: Pre-Refactorization Pivot Policy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed guard algorithm fits the leaf, but the strengthened threshold, immediate-versus-deferred refactorization branches, and associated stability policy are specialized and entirely uncited.

children.title: Refactorization-Policy Interface
children.top_down_role: Coordination between factorization state versus pivot-control policy.

assumptions_latex: The linear program is in standard form with a nonsingular current basis matrix \(B\).
A factorization state supplies solves with \(B\) and \(B^{\mathsf T}\), together with numerical diagnostics.
The policy thresholds and an exact refactorization routine are fixed before the pivot decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns either \(\mathrm{continue}\) with the existing factors or \(\mathrm{refactor}\) with newly computed factors; a failed refactorization returns \(\mathrm{singular}\) and forbids the pending pivot.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic interface between basis updates, numerical diagnostics, and full basis refactorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given factorization diagnostics \(\delta\), update count \(k\), thresholds \(\tau>0\) and \(K\in\mathbb N\), and a pending pivot, evaluate the trigger \(R=(\delta>\tau)\lor(k\ge K)\lor\mathrm{updateFailure}\). If \(R\) is false, retain the current factors and permit the pivot update. If \(R\) is true, form the current basis matrix \(B\) explicitly and compute a fresh factorization. Accept the factors only if the factorization reports full rank and passes its residual test; then reset \(k=0\). Otherwise return a singular-basis event and do not apply the pending pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy monitors factorization quality and update age, requests a fresh factorization when triggered, and blocks the pending pivot if the rebuilt basis is singular.
knowledge_statements.title: Refactorization-Policy Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the refactorization-policy leaf, but its trigger logic, residual acceptance test, and fail-closed pivot behavior are implementation-specific and have no cited source. Source support is required before the mathematical interface can be assessed reliably.

children.title: Basis Singularity Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Pivot-control responses to unreliable basis representations.

children.title: Singular Basis Events
children.top_down_role: Pivot-control responses when the basis representation is singular.

assumptions_latex: The constraint matrix is \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and a basis index set \(\mathcal B\) has cardinality \(m\).
The candidate basis matrix is \(B=A_{[:,\mathcal B]}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A singular event invalidates basic solves and therefore prevents certification of the associated simplex basis and pivot.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic boundary for loss of a valid simplex basis.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. The Simplex Method p. 11

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A singular basis event occurs exactly when \(\operatorname{rank}(B)<m\), equivalently \(\det(B)=0\) or \(\sigma_{\min}(B)=0\). At such an event, at least one of the systems \(Bx_B=b\), \(Bd=a_j\), or \(B^{\mathsf T}y=c_B\) lacks a unique solution. Consequently, the index set \(\mathcal B\) does not define a simplex basis, and no pivot whose acceptance relies on that matrix may be committed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basis event is singular when its basis matrix loses rank. Basic, direction, or dual solves then cease to be unique, so the pivot cannot be accepted.
knowledge_statements.title: Singular Basis Events

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. The Simplex Method p. 11

children.title: Nearly Singular Basis Events
children.top_down_role: Pivot-control responses when the basis representation is numerically unreliable without exact singularity.

assumptions_latex: The basis matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\) is nonsingular.
A norm, condition estimator, and warning threshold \(\kappa_{\mathrm{warn}}>1\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The event identifies a valid but numerically sensitive basis requiring guarded solves or refactorization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normwise, implementation-dependent classification of an invertible but ill-conditioned basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nearly singular basis event is declared when \(B\) remains nonsingular but \(\kappa(B)\ge\kappa_{\mathrm{warn}}\), where \(\kappa(B)=\lVert B\rVert\lVert B^{-1}\rVert\) in the selected subordinate norm. Equivalently, a reciprocal-condition estimator may declare the event when \(\widehat r(B)\le 1/\kappa_{\mathrm{warn}}\). This is a numerical classification rather than an algebraic one: \(\operatorname{rank}(B)=m\), yet perturbations in data or rounding errors can be amplified by a factor governed by \(\kappa(B)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basis is nearly singular when it is invertible but its estimated condition number crosses a prescribed warning threshold, indicating potentially severe error amplification.
knowledge_statements.title: Nearly Singular Basis Events

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind and invertible-but-ill-conditioned scope fit the leaf, but the reciprocal-condition estimator is not necessarily equivalent to the exact condition-number predicate without an estimator guarantee and decision convention. No numerical linear algebra or numerical simplex source is cited.

children.title: Singularity Classification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Tolerance-sensitive boundary between singular versus nearly singular basis classifications.

assumptions_latex: A basis matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times m}\), a rank tolerance \(\tau_{\mathrm{rank}}\ge0\), and a warning threshold \(\kappa_{\mathrm{warn}}>1\) are given.
The same scaling, norm, and singular-value or rank estimator are used for every classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed predicates form disjoint singular, nearly singular, and regular regimes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three-way numerical boundary after a fixed scaling and tolerance convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Classify \(B\) as singular when \(\sigma_{\min}(B)\le\tau_{\mathrm{rank}}\). If \(\sigma_{\min}(B)>\tau_{\mathrm{rank}}\), classify it as nearly singular when \(\kappa(B)\ge\kappa_{\mathrm{warn}}\), and regular when \(\kappa(B)<\kappa_{\mathrm{warn}}\). The equality cases belong respectively to the singular and nearly singular regimes. Because both quantities depend on scaling, norm, and finite-precision estimators, these choices are part of the classification interface and must remain fixed while bases are compared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed rank and condition thresholds partition candidate bases into singular, nearly singular, and regular regimes, with equality assigned to the more cautious class.
knowledge_statements.title: Singularity Classification Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three-way condition fits the classification-boundary leaf and is internally disjoint, but its rank threshold, scaling convention, and condition estimator define a solver-specific numerical classification. A dedicated source is needed to support this particular boundary.

children.title: Basis-Recovery Policy
children.top_down_role: Recovery choices available after unreliable basis events are identified.

assumptions_latex: The current basis is classified as singular or nearly singular.
A finite ordered collection of eligible replacement bases can be generated from the current simplex state.
Each replacement can be refactorized and checked for rank, residual, feasibility, and conditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy returns the first accepted replacement basis or terminates with numerical failure without certifying an invalid pivot.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fail-closed recovery from a basis rejected by singularity diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Generate replacement index sets \((\mathcal B_1,\ldots,\mathcal B_q)\) in the policy's prescribed order. For \(r=1,\ldots,q\), form \(B_r=A_{[:,\mathcal B_r]}\), compute a fresh factorization, and accept \(\mathcal B_r\) only if \(B_r\) has numerical rank \(m\), its solve residuals meet tolerance, \(\kappa(B_r)\le\kappa_{\mathrm{accept}}\), and the reconstructed basic solution satisfies the feasibility tolerance. On acceptance, replace the basis and recompute primal and dual quantities. If no candidate passes, terminate with numerical failure and leave the rejected pivot uncommitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery tests replacement bases in a fixed order, accepting only a well-conditioned, residual-valid, feasible refactorization; otherwise it stops without committing the rejected pivot.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Recovery Policy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the recovery-policy leaf, but generation and ordering of replacement bases, the combined acceptance predicates, and the fail-closed termination behavior are solver-specific. No source supports this particular recovery algorithm.

children.title: Sparse Candidate Scans
children.top_down_role: Pricing over structurally sparse eligibility sets.

assumptions_latex: Reduced costs \(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y\) are required only for an eligible set \(E\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus\mathcal B\).
The dual multiplier satisfies \(B^{\mathsf T}y=c_B\).
The entering rule and improvement tolerance \(\varepsilon\\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scan returns an eligible improving index or certifies that none exists within \(E\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization convention with pricing restricted to a structurally sparse eligibility set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, traverse only indices \(j\in E\), computing \(\bar c_j=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}y\) from the nonzeros of \(a_j\). Maintain the candidate prescribed by the entering rule among indices satisfying \(\bar c_j< -\varepsilon\). After all indices in \(E\) have been examined, return that candidate if one exists; otherwise return the certificate \(\bar c_j\ge-\varepsilon\) for every \(j\in E\). The latter is a restricted-pricing certificate and does not assert optimality over nonbasic indices outside \(E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scan only eligible sparse columns, retain an improving candidate under the chosen pricing rule, and otherwise certify absence of improvement within that eligibility set.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Candidate Scans

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The restricted sparse scan is appropriately an algorithm and correctly limits its certificate to the eligibility set, but no sparse-pricing source is supplied. In addition, the assumption contains the malformed sequence `\\varepsilon\\\\ge0`, which must be repaired to a properly delimited `\(\varepsilon\ge0\)` when a sourced record is submitted.

children.title: Hypersparse Pricing Regimes
children.top_down_role: Pricing that exploits exceptionally sparse intermediate vectors.

assumptions_latex: A pricing computation has active index sets \(S_v\) for every intermediate vector \(v\).
Sparse and dense kernels implement the same exact reduced-cost map.
A hypersparsity threshold \(0<\rho_{\\mathrm{hyper}}<1\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Within this regime, sparse kernels evaluate the same pricing quantities while work is indexed by active entries rather than full vector dimensions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational hypersparsity defined by active-set density across pricing intermediates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pricing call is in the hypersparse regime when every designated intermediate vector \(v\) satisfies \(\lvert S_v\rvert/d_v\le\rho_{\mathrm{hyper}}\), where \(S_v=\{i:v_i\ne0\}\) and \(d_v\) is its ambient dimension. In this regime the implementation represents and traverses \(v\) through \(S_v\), while preserving the reduced costs and entering-variable decision produced by the mathematically equivalent dense computation. The threshold is an implementation parameter and does not alter the simplex optimality conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing is hypersparse when designated intermediate vectors have active-set densities below a fixed threshold, allowing sparse traversal without changing reduced costs or pivot decisions.
knowledge_statements.title: Hypersparse Pricing Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A regime condition is suitable for this leaf, but requiring every designated intermediate vector to satisfy one density threshold is an implementation-defined notion of hypersparsity and has no source. The assumption also contains malformed LaTeX for `\(\rho_{\mathrm{hyper}}\)`.

children.title: Density-Driven Kernel Switching
children.top_down_role: Adaptive movement between sparse and dense pricing kernels.

assumptions_latex: Sparse and dense kernels compute the same pricing map for identical inputs.
The measured density is \(\rho=\lvert S\rvert/d\).
Thresholds satisfy \(0\le\rho_{\mathrm{lo}}<\rho_{\mathrm{hi}}\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hysteretic switch preserves mathematical pricing results and prevents immediate oscillation between kernels.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hysteretic sparse-to-dense switching based on measured active-set density.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the kernel mode \(M\) from the first measured density \(\rho\). Before each pricing call, if \(M=\mathrm{sparse}\) and \(\rho\ge\rho_{\mathrm{hi}}\), set \(M=\mathrm{dense}\); if \(M=\mathrm{dense}\) and \(\rho\le\rho_{\mathrm{lo}}\), set \(M=\mathrm{sparse}\); otherwise retain \(M\). Execute pricing with the selected kernel, update \(S\) and \(\rho=\lvert S\rvert/d\), and return the kernel-independent reduced costs and entering decision. The strict separation \(\rho_{\mathrm{lo}}<\rho_{\mathrm{hi}}\) supplies hysteresis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose sparse or dense pricing by active-set density, using separate upward and downward thresholds so switching does not oscillate near one boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Density-Driven Kernel Switching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The hysteretic algorithm matches the kernel-switching leaf and its threshold cases are internally coherent. However, initialization, the measured support used for the next call, and the two-threshold cost policy are implementation choices unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Column-Generation Pricing Interface
children.top_down_role: Restricted-master pricing as an externally owned candidate-generation specialization.

assumptions_latex: A restricted master minimization problem has dual vector \(y\) and currently generated columns.
An external oracle can minimize reduced cost over the admissible column family \(\mathcal P\), or provide a valid lower bound on that minimum.
The reduced-cost tolerance is \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned improving column extends the restricted master; a certified lower bound \(L\ge-\varepsilon\) certifies that no admissible omitted column has reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact delayed column generation for a minimization restricted master, with termination expressed as a reduced-cost-tolerance certificate rather than an objective-gap guarantee.

source_refs.locator: 6.1. Delayed column generation p. 232

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the restricted master and expose an optimal dual vector \(y\) to the pricing oracle. The oracle either computes \(p^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{p\in\mathcal P}\{c(p)-y^{\mathsf T}a(p)\}\) or supplies a valid lower bound \(L\) on this minimum. If a returned minimizer satisfies \(\bar c(p^\star)<-\varepsilon\), return \((a(p^\star),c(p^\star))\) as an entering-column candidate and add it to the restricted master. If the oracle certifies \(L\ge-\varepsilon\), return no column; together with restricted-master optimality, this certifies that every admissible omitted column has reduced cost at least \(-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The restricted master supplies dual prices; an external oracle returns a column whose reduced cost is below the tolerance or certifies that no admissible omitted column violates that reduced-cost threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Pricing Interface

children.title: Network-Simplex Pivot Interface
children.top_down_role: Arc pricing, leaving-arc control, and network degeneracy as externally owned specializations.

assumptions_latex: A feasible capacitated minimum-cost flow is represented by a spanning-tree basis, with nonbasic arcs fixed at lower or upper bounds.
Node potentials \(\pi\) define reduced arc costs.
An eligible entering nonbasic arc creates a unique fundamental cycle with the tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface performs a tree exchange when a tree arc blocks, performs a bound flip when the entering arc itself blocks, or reports optimality when no eligible improving arc exists.

notation.meaning: fundamental cycle created by entering arc

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree-basis pivot interface for capacitated minimum-cost flow, including tree exchanges, bound flips, and degenerate pivots.

source_refs.locator: 7.3. The network simplex algorithm p. 278

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Price eligible nonbasic arcs by \(\bar c_{ij}=c_{ij}-\pi_i+\pi_j\), with the admissible improvement sign adjusted for an arc fixed at its upper bound. If none has improving reduced cost, return optimality. Otherwise choose an entering arc \(e\), form its fundamental cycle \(C(e)\), and set \(\theta\) to the minimum residual capacity in the augmentation direction over the cycle, including the entering arc. Augment by \(\theta\) and select a blocking arc by the prescribed tie rule. If a tree arc blocks, remove it from the tree and insert \(e\); if \(e\) itself is the blocking arc, move it to its opposite bound and retain the tree. Recompute or update potentials after a tree exchange. When \(\theta=0\), record a degenerate pivot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Price nonbasic arcs and augment around the entering arc's fundamental cycle. Exchange a blocking tree arc with the entering arc, or retain the tree when the entering arc reaches its opposite bound first; record zero-step pivots as degenerate.
knowledge_statements.title: Network-Simplex Pivot Interface

children.title: Generalized-Upper-Bound Interface
children.top_down_role: Grouped-variable and structured-bound pivot control as an externally owned specialization.

assumptions_latex: Variables are partitioned into groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_q\) with constraints \(\sum_{j\in G_g}x_j\le u_g\).
Each variable has bounds \(0\le x_j\le U_j\).
The current representation supplies reduced costs and group slack states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interface returns a group-feasible entering move and its first blocking event, or certifies absence of an improving admissible grouped move.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Grouped-bound candidate and blocking-event interface for generalized upper-bound simplex variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each group \(G_g\), admit an entering direction only if it respects individual bound signs and either uses available group slack or includes a compensating decrease within \(G_g\). Price every admissible grouped direction by its objective derivative and select an improving direction using the prescribed tie rule. Compute \(\theta\) as the minimum positive step to an individual bound, exhaustion of group slack, a compensating variable's lower bound, or an ordinary basis ratio-test bound. Apply the move, update the group representation, and identify the first blocking object as leaving. If no admissible direction improves the objective beyond tolerance, return no candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Price only group-feasible directions, step to the first individual, group, compensating, or basis bound, and report the corresponding leaving object.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized-Upper-Bound Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches the generalized-upper-bound interface, but the proposed grouped directions, compensating decreases, ratio-test interaction, and leaving-object semantics depend materially on the chosen GUB formulation and basis representation. With no cited GUB source, the mathematical interface is not reliable enough for revision or acceptance.
